prose_evidence.text_as_printed: What follows is a guide to making damage macros for druids. I have played a druid for about eight months. My “Main Character” is a druid. Before I continue, I know a lot of experienced druids may read this. They will stroke their druidic beards and look at what I write with a very critical eye. They will muffle and mumble and try and pick apart my words and find mistakes! To these druids I would like to very politely tell you to go and get bent please do so! I am not precious. I welcome and will consider all feedback and correction.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Before looking at building any Druid damage macros its worthwhile analysing the druid’s combat spells. Just what does a druid have in her or his arsenal? What are the strengths and limitations of each spell? And how can you bind them all together into some sort of useful combat macro?
prose_evidence.source_html: Before looking at building any Druid damage macros its worthwhile analysing the druid’s combat spells. Just what does a druid have in her or his arsenal? What are the strengths and limitations of each spell? And how can you bind them all together into some sort of useful combat macro?

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: The druid’s damaging abilities all fall under three damage types, Arcane, Fire and Physical. The druid has many “Dots” and many direct damage spells or “Nukes” as I think of them. The druid uses up energy or phenomenon points to cast his or her spells. Some spells are instant cast, some have no cooldown and some don’t trigger the global refresh timer, but none of them have all three of the above. So lets look at them one by one.

prose_evidence.source_html: Starfall

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Global Refresh: Yes Ability Cooldown: Yes Cast build time: No Phenomenon Cost: High Damage Type: Arcane Damage Notes: Very Large Nuke Sartfall is sometimes thought of as the Druid’s signature spell. The high damage yield combined with instant cast make this THE spell that young druid’s drool over. (Ew! Drood drool?). However the high phenom cost means that you cant just fire off Starfall after Startfall and the base two minute ability cooldown stops you from doing that anyway.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Solar Flare
prose_evidence.source_html: Solar Flare

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Global Refresh: Yes Ability Cooldown: Yes Cast build time: No Phenomenon Cost: None Damage Type: Fire Damage Notes: Medium Nuke + Small Dot A great little spell, fire damage for variety, no drain on your phenomenon and instant cast. When soloing however Solar Flare is preferable as the long cast time of LB slows you down to walking speed and can mean you get interrupted a lot.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Ok we have the basic druidic abilities, but this guide is all about druid macros. Because the druid deals Fire, Arcane and Physical damage. I approached macro creating with the starting point that you will want to damage mobs that are immune, resistant or even benefit from you doing these types of damage. So what follows are my basic “No physical”,”No fire” and “No arcane” Macros.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: SOLOING (also can be used as ‘NO PHYSICAL’)
prose_evidence.source_html: SOLOING (also can be used as ‘NO PHYSICAL’)

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: /cast “Star Mantle” /itemuse “Large Mottleberry” /cast “Ulvari Burst” /itemuse “Fireseeds” /cast “Reverberate” /cast “Solar Flare” /cast “Lightning Blast”
prose_evidence.source_html:
/cast “Star Mantle”
/itemuse “Large Mottleberry”
/cast “Ulvari Burst”
/itemuse “Fireseeds”
/cast “Reverberate”
/cast “Solar Flare”
/cast “Lightning Blast”

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: This macro also serves as a general damage macro for soloing. The first time you fire this off you should automatically cast Star Mantle, your weapon clickie, Fireseeds and Solar flare as well as eating a mana berry! Pretty neat huh? Your solar flare may trigger a crit and if so the next time you hit your macro you will fire off Reverberate if not it will default to Lightning Blast which may of course itself trigger a crit. Everything else in this macro will fire off again as soon as its ability cooldown timer is over. This macro has many benefits; it’s low on mana costs and very low on phenom costs. Very useful in many situations, not least of which when you are low on phenomenon or mana. (Duh!) For mobs that are not “No physical” intersperse your physical dots in between spamming this macro. A bit more on this later.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Ok so it sucks not being able to use your arcane spells but you are not helpless. This macro pulls in the best and brightest of your non arcane arsenal. Beware, this macro has a slight weakness. Spamming it over and over again will inevitably just reapply SVT on the mob, not very efficient. Try and avoid this. Just intersperse Wild growth or even dare I say it Piercing Roots when required and you should be ok. Note: Some druids object to putting Deadly Swarm in a general damage macro. I keep it in this macro mainly because your damaging toolkit is much limited by not being able use any arcane spells. It’s a user choice thing really. Just take it out if you like and manually click it as required.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Now the first thing to note is that this macro is not very useful against No Arcane or No physical mobs. However you are lucky because not a whole lot of raid targets are like this. (yes there are some) but overall this macro is fine on raid targets. So perhaps consider this your ‘Raid Burst DPS’ macro with many non-raid uses. This macro brings in all your best ‘Specials’, all the abilities you have been saving up till its time to let loose the smackdown, including Starfall and deadly swarm. It assumes you have been given QJ by your friendly neighbourhood BM but still works without it. It also very importantly includes Ire, the only macro I would put Ire in, see my above comments on this ability for why.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Remember aggro management is YOUR responsibility too, not just your tank. It’s your job to maximise the benefit of your hate reduction abilities. Do a full aggro wipe BEFORE you burst, not after and don’t forget to use quelling wind.

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Global refresh: The second after you have cast most spells where you cannot cast anything. All your spells will be unavailable during this time, including abilities that don’t themselves trigger the global refresh. A macro will not fire off two spells with a global refresh at the same time. Druid berries, Fireseeds, weapon clickies, Ire and Quickening Jolt do not trigger the global refresh. Abilities with no global refresh usually also are instant cast which makes them very useful in macros as you can fire off many abilities with just one click.

prose_evidence.preceding_heading: Notes on terminology and making macros

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Cast time: The time it takes to cast a spell. Can range from instant cast for example Reverberate or Solar Flare, to three or four seconds (Lightning Blast) right up to ten seconds or more. (KDQ task generator). A macro will not fire off more than one spell in a single click with a cast time longer than instant.

Can range from instant cast for example Reverberate or Solar Flare, to three or four seconds (Lightning Blast) right up to ten seconds or more. (KDQ task generator). A macro will not fire off more than one spell in a single click with a cast time longer than instant.
prose_evidence.preceding_heading: Notes on terminology and making macros

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: Ability cooldown: The time it takes for this ability or spell to be available again. It can range from no cooldown to ten seconds, two minutes or even 20 hours!

prose_evidence.text_as_printed: I hope this guide helps at least some druids. Our class is oft derided for its lack of dps lack of functionality, lack of utility lack of whatever. But with a bit of care, you can find a place… and not just as a buff bot or berry vending machine. Don’t be afraid to use your phenomenon. Situational healing, burst DPS or just plain survivability CAN be real strong suits. Remember, a dead druid = no dps. I’ve been in raids where the AE is killing all the high powered sorcs and necro’s around me but I alone of the squishies can live through it.
